subtitle: Lesson 29 · Capstone: Designing a Hybrid/Multi-Cloud Architecture

steps.label: 1. Classify the data
steps.sub: Regulated PHI stays on-prem; de-identified extract is portable

steps.label: 2. Design identity first
steps.sub: One conditional access policy spans on-prem and cloud

steps.label: 3. Design the network path
steps.sub: Private ExpressRoute only, no public internet route

steps.label: 4. Limit the cloud burst job
steps.sub: Reads only the de-identified extract, never raw PHI

code:
Conditional access policy: "Claims Data Access"
  Applies to: ClaimsAnalytics-Engineers, -ServiceAccounts
  Targets: on-prem claims DB (App Proxy)
           + Azure subscription "alderney-burst-prod"
  Requires: compliant device AND MFA
  Blocks: access outside registered IP ranges
caption: The same policy governs both sides -- no weaker rule for the cloud.

eyebrow: Making the boundary structural, not just written
code:
az storage account create \
  --name stalderneyextract \
  --resource-group alderney-burst-rg \
  --public-network-access Disabled

az network private-endpoint create \
  --name pe-alderney-extract \
  --vnet-name burst-vnet --subnet private-endpoints \
  --private-connection-resource-id <storage-account-id> \
  --group-id blob
caption: No public access and a private-endpoint-only path over ExpressRoute -- raw PHI has no route to the cloud.

code:
1. What crosses the boundary?  De-identified extract only.
2. What enforces that?        Private endpoint, no public
                               access, ExpressRoute-only path.
3. Who can touch either side? One identity, one policy.
4. Where does raw PHI live?   On-prem claims DB, always.
caption: A design that can't be explained in four sentences usually isn't actually enforceable.
